sections.overview: Ciliocincta sabellariae is a microscopic marine orthonectid first described from the tube-building polychaete Sabellaria cementarium in Washington State.
sections.identification: Its ciliated adults are organized in repeated body rings and include separate male and female forms; these details require microscopic examination.
sections.habitat: The original specimens came from the San Juan Islands, where the parasite was found in its marine polychaete host.
sections.diet: It lives parasitically in the host rather than capturing free-living prey; no species-specific feeding study was located.
sections.behavior: The host can contain numerous microscopic reproductive worms, but the natural timing and transmission behavior of this parasite remain poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: The original description documented males and females in infected worms; broader orthonectid research describes a parasitic plasmodium producing ciliated reproductive stages.
sections.ecology: Its known association with Sabellaria cementarium distinguishes it from C. julini, reported from Scolelepis fuliginosa; both belong to the same small genus.
sections.conservation: Records remain too sparse to establish a population trend or conservation status for this microscopic parasite.
